title: SYSK's 2025 Shocktober Halloween Spooktacular
summary: Josh and Chuck fly solo for their 2025 Halloween "Spooktacular," reading two public-domain horror stories aloud with commentary. First is E. F. Benson's "Caterpillars" (from the anthology The Room in the Tower and Other Stories), about a house guest at the Villa Caskana in Italy who encounters foot-long, crab-pincered caterpillars that appear linked to cancer. Second is "The Deep Drowse" by Alison B. Harding (a pen name, possibly Gene Milligan, Lamont Buchanan, or a husband-wife team), published in Weird Tales in September 1949: a hay-fever-suffering writer, Arthur Hodges, and his wife Fran seal themselves in an air-conditioned study, then find their friends and the town stricken by a mysterious drowsiness, and the story ends with a far-future hieroglyphic-report twist. The episode includes a sponsor-free reading format, banter about the stories and household tips, and a sign-off.
topics: Planet of the Apes style ending

segments.title: Halloween Spooktacular opening
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck open the 2025 Halloween episode, introduce the tradition of reading two stories, and plug guest producer Ben's music.

segments.title: Introducing E. F. Benson's Caterpillars
segments.summary: The hosts identify the story as E. F. Benson's 'Caterpillars' from The Room in the Tower and Other Stories and discuss its setting.
topics: The Room in the Tower and Other Stories

segments.title: Reading 'Caterpillars'
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck read Benson's story: a guest at the Villa Caskana on the Italian Riviera sees luminous, crab-footed caterpillars covering a bed in an unoccupied room, which later swarm the house. The hosts remark on the creepy turn and on pronunciation of Italian words.

segments.title: Off-topic household tips
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck banter about cleaning marble and limestone with a baking soda poultice for wine stains.

segments.title: Caterpillars continued and ending
segments.summary: The narrator throws a caterpillar in a pill box into a fountain, sees it survive and swim, and watches the swarm return at night. The story closes with a rooms-with-cancer reveal from the hostess, which the hosts interpret as the caterpillars carrying cancer, and they conclude it is a real experience.

segments.title: Introducing The Deep Drowse and its author
segments.summary: Chuck introduces 'The Deep Drowse' from Weird Tales (September 1949) by pen name Alison B. Harding, and the hosts discuss the author's mystery, with Gene Milligan suggested as a possible identity.

segments.title: Reading 'The Deep Drowse' part one
segments.summary: The story introduces Arthur Hodges, a writer with bad hay fever who lives in a country house with a hermetically sealed study and bedroom. His wife Fran and friends get calls that sound drugged. Arthur calls the police, a doctor, and friends, and reaches a caretaker who is found collapsed outside. Arthur goes outside briefly and feels sleepy.

segments.title: The Deep Drowse: the couple in the cave
segments.summary: Arthur and Fran shelter in the sealed cave-like room, rationing food and oxygen as the outside world seems silent. Arthur writes a chronicle on a typewriter. They decide to go outside and collapse on the lawn.

segments.title: The Deep Drowse conclusion and wrap-up
segments.summary: Chuck reads the far-future hieroglyphic report explaining the event as a drowsiness caused by a change in the atmosphere that led to starvation, and the last human captured by animal jurors. Josh and Chuck comment on the ending and sign off wishing listeners a happy Halloween.
